text:
sasha: Heads up — noticing a ~5% subset of inference requests in us-west2 where trace_id disappears between ingress and gpu-proxy after the deploy. Kibana shows X-Request-Id present but our trace_id field empty. Anyone else seeing gaps? :thinking:

jia: Which header are you tracking? are you looking at `trace_id` field in the json logs or HTTP header like `x-trace-id`?

sasha: Logs: our app emits `trace_id` and `req_id`. Example from frontend logs: `req_id=abc123 trace_id=1a2b3c` but downstream gpu-proxy logs show `req_id=abc123 trace_id=` (empty).

omar: Could be header rewriting at the egress proxy (envoy). We had `header_format_sanitizer` rolled out last week that lowercases/removes some grpc metadata headers.

kevin: Do we have a quick Loki query to find affected flows? Trying now.

omar: Try this Loki query (gpu-proxy namespace):
```
{job="gpu-proxy", region="us-west2"} |= "req_id=" | regexp "req_id=\"(?P<req>[^\"]+)\".*trace_id=\"(?P<tr>[^\"]*)\""
```
This shows lines where trace_id is empty (`tr==""`).

jia: In Kibana you can use KQL: `service.name: "gpu-proxy" and not has:trace_id` to get docs missing the field. Also try `exists:trace_id == false`.

kevin: I ran the Loki query — about 1200 hits in the last 30m, almost all from the same node pool (gpu-pool-usw2-a).

alert-bot: "[ALERT] central-logs-missing-traceid fired (severity: warning) — 5% of requests missing trace_id in last 10m. Link: https://pager.redwood/alerts/central-logs-missing-traceid"

omar: That node pool was on the same kernel/Envoy revision from the canary. Looks like the envoy bump enabled `strip_matching_headers` for `x-*` patterns. If that removed `x-trace-id` header we lose mapping.

sasha: Possible repro: curl to ingress with `X-Trace-Id: t-123` and follow logs. Can someone port-forward gpu-proxy and tail logs?

kevin: Reproduced locally — ingress receives header, but envoy to backend has transformed `x-trace-id` -> `x-trace-id` (same) but grpc metadata `grpc-trace-bin` got dropped. Our tracing library maps `grpc-trace-bin` -> trace_id.

jia: Suggested short-term mitigation: update Loki/Kibana queries and SLO alert to only count requests where req latency > 100ms (reduce noise), and add a rule to correlate on `req_id` if `trace_id` missing so we can still stitch spans.

omar: Long-term fix: patch envoy config to preserve `grpc-trace-bin` and disable header sanitizer for the route, or add `copy_request_headers` mapping to copy `x-trace-id` into `traceparent` header which our stack always reads.

kevin: Patch ready as a flag in the envoy config: `preserve_grpc_trace_bin: true` — smoke-tested in staging, looks green. I'll open PR and target a rolling restart for gpu-pool-usw2-a.

sasha: Nice. After deploy, let's run this Loki check and post counts. Also update alert to be `>=3% for 10m` instead of current 1% to avoid thrash.

omar: I'll handle the PR and the rollback plan if we see any spike.

kevin: Post-deploy Loki query to verify:
```
{job="gpu-proxy", region="us-west2"} |= "req_id=" | json | (has("trace_id") and trace_id != "") | count_over_time(10m)
```
Compare with total reqs to compute percent.

sasha: Great. Thanks team — leaving the alert on watch. Will update when PR lands and after patch. :white_check_mark:
